payload.prompt: Total costs increased significantly from January to February 2026. Analyze the general ledger and identify the three expense accounts with the largest increase in amount. Create an internal project for each of the three accounts using the account name. Also create an activity for each project.

payload.goal: Analyze the general ledger for January vs February 2026, identify the three expense accounts with the largest cost increase, then create one internal project per account (named after the account) and one activity per project.
success_checks: General ledger queried for period 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-31 and 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28
Three expense accounts with largest month-over-month increase identified and ranked
Three internal projects created, each named after one of the identified expense accounts
One activity created and linked to each of the three projects
All projects marked as internal (not customer-facing)
risk_notes: Sandbox is empty — no ledger data exists yet; real ledger data must be present for analysis to yield meaningful results
Expense account classification depends on chart of accounts structure (typically accounts 4000–7999 in Norwegian accounting); clarification may be needed
If multiple accounts have equal increases, tie-breaking rule is undefined — risk of ambiguity in selection
Activity type/name not specified in prompt; a generic default activity name will be used per project
Project manager not specified; projects may require a responsible employee — risk of validation error if mandatory
Start/end dates for projects not provided; may be required fields in Tripletex
VAT not applicable to this task
payload.suggested_first_action: GET /ledger?dateFrom=2026-01-01&dateTo=2026-02-28&fields=account,amount to retrieve ledger postings for both months, then aggregate by expense account to compute the delta.
ordered_steps: 1. GET /ledger/account?fields=id,number,name,type to retrieve full chart of accounts and identify expense account ranges
4. Aggregate total debit amounts per expense account for January and February respectively
5. Compute delta (February total minus January total) per expense account
6. Sort accounts by delta descending and select the top three
7. POST /project for project #1: name=<account1_name>, isInternal=true, set required fields (startDate, projectManager if mandatory)
8. POST /project/activity for project #1: link activityId or create generic activity named after account1
10. POST /project/activity for project #2: link/create activity named after account2
12. POST /project/activity for project #3: link/create activity named after account3
13. Verify all three projects and their activities are visible via GET /project?fields=id,name,activities

planned_endpoints.summary: Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Find employees corresponding with sent data.

rules: When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
Requires name and departmentNumber.
ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'NO_ACCESS' (safest default — avoids 422 errors). Only use 'STANDARD' if email login is explicitly needed.
startDate is a TOP-LEVEL field on the employee object. Do NOT put it inside an employments array.
dateOfBirth is a TOP-LEVEL field. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
jobTitle is set via PUT /employee/{id} AFTER creation — it cannot be set in the initial POST.
Do NOT include an 'employments' array in POST /employee — employment details go via separate POST /employee/employment endpoint.

For occupation codes (STYRK/yrkeskode): POST /employee/employment first, then GET /employee/employment/occupationCode?nameAndCode=XXXX to find the code, then PUT /employee/employment/details to set it.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id} and projectManager={"id": employee_id}.
startDate is REQUIRED — set to 2026-01-01 or earlier to allow timesheet entries on any date.
If the prompt mentions a project number (prosjektnummer), set number=<project_number>.
isInternal should be false unless explicitly stated as internal project.
For project BUDGET (budsjett/orçamento): use fixedprice=<amount> (this is the budget field in Tripletex).
For fixed-price projects, also set isFixedPrice=true.
Requires project={"id": project_id} and activity={"id": activity_id}.
If activity already linked (409), ignore the error and proceed.
If a default hourly rate already exists (409 Duplicate entry), GET /project/hourlyRates?projectId=... then PUT to update it.
For fixed rate: hourlyRateModel='TYPE_FIXED_HOURLY_RATE', fixedRate=<rate>.

payload.headline: Wrong top-3 expense accounts identified; only 1/5 scoring checks passed despite successful project creation
what_went_wrong: Ledger analysis produced incorrect top-3 accounts — scoring checks 2-5 failed, suggesting the agent misidentified which accounts had the largest increase (possibly wrong aggregation logic or missed postings).
aggregate_endpoint tool returned 0 groups for both account.number and account.id groupings, forcing manual raw-data parsing which is error-prone and likely caused incorrect totals.
Used wrong activity type initially ($REF:activity_Administrasjon is GENERAL_ACTIVITY, not PROJECT_GENERAL_ACTIVITY), causing 3 unnecessary 422 errors before switching to Prosjektadministrasjon.
Duplicate API calls throughout: every aggregate_endpoint and GET /ledger/posting call was issued twice simultaneously, doubling unnecessary API usage without benefit.
what_worked: Project creation succeeded for all 3 accounts with correct isInternal=true flag.
Self-corrected activity type error by fetching /activity and switching to Prosjektadministrasjon.
what_to_try_next: Verify ledger aggregation by fetching ALL postings with pagination (count=500) and explicitly filtering for expense account range 4000-7999, then re-check the delta calculations — the current analysis likely missed some postings.
Pre-check activity types before creating projectActivity records: filter GET /activity for isProjectActivity=true to avoid the 3 wasted 422 calls.
Eliminate duplicate parallel tool calls — each aggregate_endpoint and GET call was issued twice; remove the redundant duplicates to halve unnecessary API usage and improve efficiency score.
unnecessary_calls: Duplicate aggregate_endpoint calls (8 total for 4 unique queries) — each was issued twice simultaneously with identical params
GET /ledger/posting (no params) called twice as raw inspection — one call sufficient
3x POST /project/projectActivity with wrong activity_Administrasjon — avoidable with upfront activity type check
